items.headline: U.S. Stocks End Mixed as AI Momentum Lifts Markets Amidst Yield & Oil Concerns
items.summary: U.S. equities closed mixed on Friday, September 25, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average recording its third consecutive day of losses, while the Nasdaq Composite managed a marginal gain and the S&P 500 finished nearly flat. This mixed performance came as investors weighed surging Treasury yields, elevated crude oil prices, and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East against a strong underlying economy, primarily driven by AI advancements. Consumer sentiment, despite being at a four-month low, was not as bad as economists expected.

items.headline: Akamai Technologies Surges on Cloud Services Deal
items.summary: Akamai Technologies ($AKAM) surged 15.31% after the cybersecurity company announced a seven-year, $11.6 billion cloud services commitment from AI company Anthropic.

items.headline: People Inc. Jumps on Potential MGM Bid
items.summary: Digital media and holding company People Incorporated ($PPLI) jumped 10.27% following reports that MGM Resorts International is considering a takeover bid.

items.headline: Dell Technologies Up on AI Server Demand
items.summary: Dell Technologies Inc. ($DELL) opened up by 3.63% as shares rebounded from insider selling pressures amid strong AI server demand and raised full-year guidance.

items.headline: Twilio Drops on Analyst Downgrade
items.summary: Twilio ($TWLO) lost 4.41% after HSBC downgraded the cloud communications company to 'reduce' from 'hold'.

items.headline: Zscaler Tumbles Amidst Management Changes
items.summary: Zscaler ($ZS) tumbled 9% on news of management changes.

items.headline: Meta Platforms Down Amidst Volatile Market
items.summary: Meta Platforms ($META) was down 3.51% today, drawing attention from Wall Street amidst continued market volatility.

items.headline: Sector Performance Mixed: Communication Services and Healthcare Lead, Materials and Utilities Lag
items.summary: Communication services and healthcare stocks were the biggest gainers today, with the Communication Services Select Sector SPDR (XLC) gaining 1.3% and the Health Care Select Sector SPDR (XLV) adding 0.6%. Conversely, materials and utilities stocks were the worst performers, as the Utilities Select Sector SPDR (XLU) lost 1% and the Materials Select Sector SPDR (XLB) fell 1.2%. Eight of the 11 S&P 500 sectors ended in negative territory.

items.headline: Key Economic Data Released: Jobless Claims Decline, New Home Sales Jump
items.summary: The Labor Department reported that jobless claims totaled 197,000 for the week ending September 19, a decrease of 1,000 from the previous week's revised level. U.S. new home sales jumped 6.4% in August to a seasonally adjusted annualized rate of 684,000 units, reaching the highest level since December 2025.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Surge on Rate Hike Fears; Fed Watch Indicates High Probability of October Hike
items.summary: Bond yields continued their upward trend, with the 30-year Treasury yield jumping to 5.501%, its highest level since June 2004, and the 10-year Treasury yield reaching 5.223%, the highest since June 2007. Markets are pricing in a 71% chance of a rate hike by the Federal Reserve in its October policy meeting, up from 66% a day ago, driven by fears of further interest rate increases.

items.headline: Q2 2026 Earnings Show Strong Performance, Especially Outside Energy Sector
items.summary: For Q2 2026, year-over-year earnings are expected to be 53.7%, with 86.1% of S&P 500 companies reporting above analyst expectations so far for Q1 2026. Excluding the energy sector, the year-over-year earnings estimate is 49.8%.

items.headline: Geopolitical Risks and Oil Prices Continue to Influence Market Sentiment
items.summary: Uncertainty about the Middle East continued to dent investor sentiment, with crude oil prices falling today as markets weighed developments in the U.S.-Iran conflict. Brent oil prices dropped 2.8% to US$97.44 per barrel, influenced by hopes for a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
